known.title: Research says that one closing keyword closes every issue of a comma list, so `Closes #18, #20` leaves #20 open after the merge and archive of this plan refuses
known.summary: The landing bullet says that GitHub applies one closing keyword to each issue number of a comma list, so the pull request line `Closes #18, #20` closes both plans at merge. The GitHub page that the plan cites (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue) gives the syntax for multiple issues as 'Use full syntax for each issue', for example `Resolves #10, resolves #123`. So only #18 closes, and #20 stays open after the merge. At repo_ref, plan-manager/SKILL.md line 203 says that `archive <issue>` requires completed closure, so the lifecycle of this plan cannot finish. The line must repeat the keyword for each issue (`Closes #18`, `Closes #20`).

known.title: Research maps `gh pr checks` exit 8 to a failed check, but the GitHub CLI manual defines exit 8 as checks pending, so the landing rule blocks on pending checks and does not detect failed checks by exit status
known.locator: Research, gh pr checks exit-status bullet (lines 37-40); Steps, row 1 combined_contract, Done when (line 49)
known.summary: The exit-status bullet says that `gh pr checks` exits 8 when a check failed, and the bounded check discovery of step 1 treats exit 8 as a failed check that blocks the merge and retries exit 1 as an API error. The manual page that the plan cites (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_checks) lists one additional exit code: '8: Checks pending'. So the contract of step 1 reports a pending check as a failed check, and it gives no exit status that identifies a failed check: a failed run goes to the retry path for errors and then to a no-checks blocker. The check policy must read the `bucket` field of `--json` (pass, fail, pending, skipping, cancel) or treat exit 8 as pending.

known.title: Acceptance landing-pr greps the contract for `Closes #<issue>`, which the contract already holds three times at repo_ref, so the row passes when step 1 adds no landing rule
known.locator: Acceptance, row landing-pr (line 58); Steps, row 1 combined_contract (line 49)
known.summary: Row landing-pr expects at least one match of `Closes #<issue>` in plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md as the proof that the contract tells the manager to open the closing pull request after `Code-review: pass` (the routine landing of step 1). At repo_ref the contract already holds the string at lines 137, 250, and 254, in text that leaves the landing to the user (plan-manager/SKILL.md line 152: the user has landed the closing pull request). So `grep -c` prints 3 before any change, and the row passes when step 1 does not change the landing rule. The row must check text that only the new rule holds.

known.title: Step 3 refreshes the content hashes after step 1 only, but step 2 edits a plan-workspace reference that the plan-workspace hash covers, so the hash can go stale after the refresh
known.locator: Steps, row 3 hashes_and_gate, Depends (line 51); Steps, row 2 regression_contract, Files (line 50)
known.summary: Step 3 refreshes the skill content hashes and runs the gate, and it depends only on step 1. Step 2 also edits plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-workspace/references/codex-agent-templates.md. At repo_ref, scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs (hashSkill, lines 73-88) hashes SKILL.md plus every sorted references/*.md of the skill, and scripts/ci.mjs (lines 520-522) fails on content_hash drift. So step 3 can run before step 2, refresh the plan-workspace hash for the old template bytes, and pass its gate; step 2 then changes the template, and the stored hash no longer matches. Step 3 must depend on step 2.
